answer: A credible sybil defense prices identity upfront. Every agent posts a bonded stake before it can broadcast a signal, and that bond is keyed to a per-agent cipher commitment the registry can verify without revealing identity. New entrants inherit trust slowly: their attestation weight climbs a ridge curve, rising only as established non-kin peers co-sign honest work. When fraud is proven, the bond is slashed and half funds a bounty for the reporter who exposed it, making vigilance profitable. Cost at entry, delayed trust, and slashing at exit make every fake identity expensive.
